newsitem.title: USA: Horizon agrees to be bought by Compass.
newsitem.headline: Horizon agrees to be bought by Compass.

text.p: Horizon Bancorp Inc said Thursday that it and its subsidiary, Horizon Bank & Trust, SSB, have signed a letter of intent to be bought by Compass Bancshares Inc.

Terms call for Compass to exchange shares of its common stock for all of the outstanding common stock of Horizon Bancorp, Horizon said. The transaction is expected to be completed during the first half of 1997.
The deal marks Compass's entry into the Austin market and will add $144 million in assets and eight locations to Compass's Texas franchise, Horizon said.
"Entering Austin has been a priority of Compass's Texas strategy," Charles McMahen, chief executive of Compass's Compass Banks of Texas Inc, said in a statement.

The acquisition would increase Compass's banking offices to 100 and raise its assets to more than $4.8 billion statewide, including the pending acquisitions of Texas American Bank in San Antonio and ProBank in Houston, Horizon said.
Horizon said Douglas Kadison, its chief executive and chairman, and Paul Antrim, its executive vice president and chief financial officer, will remain part of Compass's management.
Compass is a $10.8 billion bank holding company that reported earnings of $67.4 million for the first six months of 1996, Horizon said. It has a capital base of $701 million, the company said.
Trading for Horizon was halted 11:36 EDT at 17.
